label: Make public, no crossplay
summary: Makes the multiplayer lobby public without allowing crossplay.
details: Going by its name and its use as a button click in the multiplayer setup GUI, it presumably switches the lobby to a public game with crossplay turned off. The game does not say more. It returns nothing.

label: Show player list
summary: Switches the multiplayer lobby between its player list and its game settings.
details: It returns nothing and takes one yes or no value. Vanilla passes yes from the 'Players' tab and no from the game settings tab.

fields.name: argument 1
fields.text: Whether to show the player list (no shows the game settings).

label: DLC list open
summary: Whether the multiplayer lobby's list of enabled DLCs is opened.
details: Vanilla shows the list and its close button while it is yes, and the open button while it is no; ToggleShowEnabledDLCs switches it.

label: Mod list open
summary: Whether the multiplayer lobby's list of enabled mods is opened.
details: Vanilla shows the list and its close button while it is yes, and the open button while it is no; ToggleShowEnabledMods switches it.

label: Show hosting part
summary: Whether the hosting part of the multiplayer lobby should be shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility condition of a part of the multiplayer lobby GUI. What that part is (perhaps the host controls) follows from the name only.

label: Show modify server
summary: Whether the option to modify the server settings should be shown in the lobby.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Show player list
summary: Whether the lobby currently shows the player list instead of the settings.
details: Vanilla combines it with the lobby tab setting and with whether server info exists: the player list part is visible when it is yes, and the settings part when it is no.

label: Start game
summary: Starts the multiplayer game from the lobby.
details: Vanilla calls it from a button click in the multiplayer lobby. Going by its name, it launches the session. It returns nothing.

label: Start button tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the lobby's start button.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of a button in the multiplayer lobby GUI. That it is the start button follows from the name. It returns text.

label: Toggle auto accept
summary: Switches automatic acceptance of joining players on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the multiplayer setup GUI. The meaning (players who ask to join are let in without the host's approval) follows from the name and a related setting named hotjoin auto accept.

label: Toggle observe
summary: Switches the local player between observing and playing in the lobby.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the multiplayer lobby window. The exact effect follows from the name only.

label: Toggle DLC list
summary: Opens or closes the multiplayer lobby's list of enabled DLCs.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the list's open and close buttons.

label: Toggle mod list
summary: Opens or closes the multiplayer lobby's list of enabled mods.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the list's open and close buttons.

label: Toggle game visibility
summary: Switches a hosted multiplayer game between private (invite only) and public.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from both the 'private' and the 'public' boxes of the multiplayer setup, which show the server's IsInvite and IsPublic state.

label: Cancel ready
summary: Takes the local player back out of the ready state in the lobby.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Activity data itself
summary: Gives the local player's activity data object itself.
details: Going by its name and by the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on, so it can be passed on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Completion effects text
summary: The text describing what completing the activity gives.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the activity window and shows that text block only when it is not empty. That the text lists what completing the activity gives follows from the name only.

label: Activity data itself
summary: Gives the local player's activity data object itself.
details: Going by its name and by how the same name is used on other types (for example as an argument, as in a character's Self). The game documents nothing more.

label: Activity data
summary: The local player's activity data.
details: The one vanilla line found (the activity window setting its data context) names the function through another type path, so it is only a hint that the activity window reads this data.

label: Court events data
summary: The local player's court events data.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the main screen (the HUD), which also reads court event numbers.

label: New artifacts data
summary: The local player's record of new artifacts.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the main screen (the HUD), which also reads new artifact numbers.

label: Cached data itself
summary: Gives the local player's cached data object itself.
details: Going by its name and the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Situation data
summary: The local player's situation data.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the main screen (the HUD), which also reads the numbers of new situations, stories and struggles.

label: Triggered legend seeds
summary: The list of legend seeds that have been triggered for the local player.
details: Vanilla adds its item count to the count of the character's own legend seeds in the "You have N legend seeds" text, and a HUD part is visible when either list has items. What counts as triggered follows from the name only.

label: Has opened royal court
summary: Whether the local player has ever opened the royal court window.
details: Vanilla combines it with the check for the character having a royal court: a HUD part is visible when the character has a court that was never opened (or when another court-event condition holds).

label: Cached data itself
summary: Gives the local player's cached data object itself.
details: Going by its name and by how the same name is used on other types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Court events itself
summary: Gives the local player's court events object itself.
details: Going by its name and the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Court event count
summary: The number of court events the local player has not handled yet.
details: Vanilla shows it in the royal court status text ("unhandled" events) and compares it with a number to decide whether a HUD part is shown.

label: Court events itself
summary: Gives the local player's court events object itself.
details: Going by its name and by how the same name is used on other types. The game documents nothing more.

label: New artifacts itself
summary: Gives the local player's new artifacts record itself.
details: Going by its name and the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Clear new artifacts
summary: Clears the "new" mark from all the local player's new artifacts.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it. It returns nothing.

label: Clear new artifacts of category
summary: Clears the "new" mark from the new artifacts of one category.
details: Vanilla calls it with 'court' from clicks in the inventory window. Presumably this clears the new marks of the court category.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact category, written as text.

label: New artifact count
summary: The number of new artifacts the local player has.
details: Vanilla shows it as a number in the royal court window and in a status text ("You have N new ...").

label: New artifacts in category
summary: The number of new artifacts in one category.
details: Vanilla asks it for the 'court' category, in the royal court status text and in a condition of the HUD.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact category, written as text.

label: New artifacts in slot
summary: The number of new artifacts that belong in one inventory slot.
details: Vanilla uses it in the inventory window with the slot's type string, to show a number on the slot, only when the viewed character is the local player.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The slot type, as the slot's type string.
fields.values: a text, for example from the inventory slot's type string

label: Has new artifacts
summary: Whether the local player has any new artifacts.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Is new artifact
summary: Whether the given artifact is marked as new for the local player.
details: Vanilla uses it in the inventory window as a visibility condition for something shown on an artifact (presumably a "new" marker).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an artifact, such as the current artifact of the GUI

label: Remove new mark
summary: Removes the "new" mark from one artifact.
details: Vanilla calls it on a right click on an artifact in the holy site window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact whose mark is removed.

label: New artifacts itself
summary: Gives the local player's new artifacts record itself.
details: Going by its name and by how the same name is used on other types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Situation data itself
summary: Gives the local player's situation data object itself.
details: Going by its name and the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: New situation count
summary: The number of new situations.
details: Vanilla adds it to the new story and new struggle counts for the situations number in the HUD, and uses it in the "New situations" tooltip text (singular or plural).

label: New story count
summary: The number of new stories.
details: Vanilla adds it to the new situation and new struggle counts for the HUD number, and uses it in the "New stories" tooltip text.

label: New struggle count
summary: The number of new struggles.
details: Vanilla adds it to the new situation and new story counts for the HUD number, and uses it in the "New struggles" tooltip text.

label: Has any new situation
summary: Whether there is anything new among the situations.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility condition of a HUD part. That it covers every kind (situations, stories, struggles) follows from its name only.

label: Has new situations
summary: Whether there are new situations.
details: Vanilla combines it with the checks for new stories and new struggles as a visibility and trigger condition of a HUD part, and uses it to add the "New situations" line to the situations button text.

label: Has new stories
summary: Whether there are new stories.
details: Vanilla combines it with the checks for new situations and new struggles as a visibility and trigger condition of a HUD part.

label: Has new struggles
summary: Whether there are new struggles.
details: Vanilla combines it with the checks for new situations and new stories as a visibility and trigger condition of a HUD part.

label: Situation data itself
summary: Gives the local player's situation data object itself.
details: Going by its name and by how the same name is used on other types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Log entry itself
summary: Gives the log entry object itself.
details: Going by its name and the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Log entry color
summary: The color of a log entry.
details: Going by its name and its return type (a four-part color vector), it gives the color the entry is drawn in. Vanilla does not use it on log entries; other types use a function of the same name for colors.

label: Log entry text
summary: The text of a log entry.
details: Going by its name and its return type (text). Vanilla does not use it on log entries.

label: Log entry time
summary: The time of a log entry, as text.
details: Going by its name and its return type (text). Vanilla does not use it.

label: Log entry itself
summary: Gives the log entry object itself.
details: Going by its name and by how the same name is used on other types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Log categories
summary: The list of categories of the log viewer.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla does not use it on the log viewer; the music player has a function of the same name that serves as a list source in the GUI.

label: Log viewer itself
summary: Gives the log viewer object itself.
details: Going by its name and the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Log types
summary: The list of message types of the engine's log viewer.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list (`datamodel`) twice: buttons that open the log viewer filtered to one type, and boxes that switch a type's filter, each with the type's icon and count. The game does not register its return type.

label: Shrink log info
summary: Makes the log info box of the engine's log viewer smaller.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from a button with the tooltip 'Decrease size of the log info box'.

label: Flush log
summary: Flushes the log of the engine's log viewer.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from a button with the tooltip 'Flush log'. Whether that clears the shown entries or writes them out is not shown.

label: Filtered entry count
summary: The number of log entries left after filtering.
details: Going by its name and its number return type. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Last log entry
summary: The newest entry of the engine's log viewer.
details: Vanilla uses it on a right-click of the 'Show Log Viewer' button, opening that entry in the external log viewer. The game does not register its return type.

label: Log info size
summary: The size of the expanded info area of the log viewer, as a whole number.
details: Going by its name and its number return type. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Log info size
summary: The size (width and height) of the log viewer's log info box.
details: It takes one decimal number; vanilla passes 60 and uses the result as the size of the box. What the number does (a base size or a step) is not shown. The increase and decrease buttons change the size.

fields.name: argument 1
fields.text: A number the size is worked out from; its meaning is not shown.

label: Selected log entry
summary: The entry selected in the engine's log viewer.
details: Vanilla shows its time, file, line and message in the log info box, and offers to open it in the script editor (when it names a script file), the code editor or the external log viewer. The game does not register its return type.

label: Search text
summary: The text in the search field of the engine's log viewer.
details: Vanilla shows it in the 'Search:' field; finishing the edit sets it with SetTextFilter, and a button clears it with ResetTextFilter.

label: Has entries
summary: Whether the log viewer has any entries.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Grow log info
summary: Makes the log info box of the engine's log viewer larger.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from a button with the tooltip 'Give more space to the log info box'.

label: Entry selected
summary: Whether an entry is selected in the engine's log viewer.
details: Vanilla shows the log info box only when this is yes.

label: Show log viewer
summary: Opens the engine's log viewer.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from a button with the tooltip 'Show Log Viewer'; a right-click on the same button opens the newest entry in the external log viewer instead.

label: Show log of one type
summary: Opens the engine's log viewer filtered to one message type.
details: It returns nothing and takes one value: vanilla passes the id of a log type (`LogViewerType.GetId`) from a row of type buttons, each with the tooltip 'Show Log Viewer …' and the type's name.

fields.name: argument 1
fields.text: The id of the message type to show.
fields.values: a log type id, as vanilla writes `LogViewerType.GetId`

label: Reset log filters
summary: Clears the filters of the log viewer.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla does not use it on the log viewer; the ledger window has a function of the same name that is called from a click.

label: Reset search text
summary: Clears the search text of the engine's log viewer.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from a button with the tooltip 'Reset text filter' next to the search field.

label: Log viewer itself
summary: Gives the log viewer object itself.
details: Going by its name and by how the same name is used on other types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set search text
summary: Takes the text typed into the log viewer's search field as its filter.
details: It returns nothing and takes no argument. Vanilla runs it when editing of the 'Search:' field is finished, so it reads the value from that field.

label: Toggle hidden
summary: Switches the log viewer between hidden and shown.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Log category itself
summary: Gives the log category object itself.
details: Going by its name and the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Filtered count
summary: The number of entries of this log category left after filtering.
details: Going by its name and its number return type. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Category icon
summary: The icon of this log category.
details: Going by its name, and by other types where a function of this name gives an icon used as a texture. Vanilla does not use it on log categories.

label: Is filtered
summary: Whether this log category is currently filtered.
details: Going by its name only. It is not clear from the input whether yes means shown or hidden. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Category name
summary: The name of this log category.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. Vanilla does not use it on log categories; other types use a function of this name for display names.

label: Log category itself
summary: Gives the log category object itself.
details: Going by its name and by how the same name is used on other types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set filtered
summary: Sets whether this log category is filtered.
details: Going by its name only. It takes one value that the game does not describe, presumably yes or no. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Log entry itself
summary: Gives the log viewer entry object itself.
details: Going by its name and the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Names a script file
summary: Whether an entry of the engine's log viewer points to a script file.
details: Vanilla shows an extra mark on the entry's row when this is yes; for the selected entry, the same check shows the 'Open in script editor' button.

label: Line number
summary: The line number in the file that the log entry points to.
details: Going by its name and its number return type. Vanilla does not use it.

label: File name
summary: The name of the file that the log entry points to.
details: Going by its name only. The return type is not registered in the game's data. Vanilla does not use it on log entries.

label: File path
summary: The path of the file that the log entry points to, as text.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Entry icon
summary: The icon of an entry of the engine's log viewer.
details: Vanilla uses it as a picture on the entry's row. What the icon stands for is not shown. The game does not register its return type.

label: Entry message
summary: The message text of an entry of the engine's log viewer.
details: Vanilla shows it on the entry's row after its short time stamp.

label: Long timestamp
summary: The time of this log entry in a long written form.
details: Going by its name and its text return type; the exact format is not given. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Short timestamp
summary: The time of this log entry, written in a short form.
details: Belongs to the log viewer, the game's tool window that lists error and log messages. Vanilla shows it at the start of each log row, followed by the entry's message; the selected entry's details use a long timestamp instead.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this log entry is selected in the log viewer.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of each row in the log viewer (the game's tool window for error and log messages); clicking the row flips it with SetSelected.

label: Open in code editor
summary: Opens the file of this log entry in a code editor.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it. It returns nothing.

label: Open in editor
summary: Opens this log entry in an editor.
details: Vanilla calls it from the button on each log row (tooltip "Open in editor (or: right-click row)") and when the row is right-clicked. The selected entry's info box has separate buttons for a script editor and a code editor; which one this function uses is not stated.

label: Open in external viewer
summary: Opens this log entry in an external log viewer program.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Open in script editor
summary: Opens the script file of this log entry in a script editor.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Log entry itself
summary: Gives the log viewer entry object itself.
details: Going by its name and by how the same name is used on other types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set selected
summary: Selects or deselects this log entry in the log viewer.
details: Vanilla calls it when a log row is clicked, passing the opposite of IsSelected, so a click toggles the selection.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether the entry should be selected.

label: Log type itself
summary: Gives the log type object itself.
details: Going by its name and the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Filtered count
summary: A number of log entries of this log type, shown on the type's button in the log viewer.
details: Vanilla shows it next to the type's icon, both on the small counter buttons and on the filter buttons of the log viewer. Going by its name, it counts the entries left after filtering; the game does not say more.

label: Log type icon
summary: The icon of this log type.
details: Vanilla draws it as a small 16 by 16 icon on the log type's counter and filter buttons in the log viewer.

label: Log type id
summary: The number that identifies this log type.
details: Vanilla passes it to LogViewer.OpenLinkedLogViewerFilteredByType, so clicking a log type's counter button opens the log viewer showing only that type (the button's tooltip: "Show Log Viewer" and the type's name).

label: Is filtered
summary: Whether the log viewer's filter is switched on for this log type.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the log type's filter button, with the type's name as tooltip; clicking flips it with SetIsFiltered. Whether pressed means the type is shown or hidden is not stated.

label: Log type name
summary: The name of this log type.
details: Vanilla shows it in the tooltips of the log viewer's type buttons, for example "Show Log Viewer" followed by the name.

label: Log type itself
summary: Gives the log type object itself.
details: Going by its name and by how the same name is used on other types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set filtered
summary: Switches the log viewer's filter on or off for this log type.
details: Vanilla calls it from the type's filter button, passing the opposite of GetIsFiltered, so a click toggles it. Whether on means the type is shown or hidden is not stated.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether the filter is on for this type.

label: Login view itself
summary: Gives the login view object itself.
details: Going by its name and the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Email
summary: The email address in the login window.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the login window of the Paradox account.

label: Login error message
summary: The error message of the login window.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the login window of the Paradox account.

label: Login text
summary: The login name text shown in the login window.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the login window. What exactly it holds (account name or email) follows from the name only.

label: Password
summary: The password entered in the login window.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the login window. Going by the name it is the password text typed so far.

label: Close login window
summary: Hides the login window.
details: Vanilla calls it from clicks (close buttons) in the login window.

label: Is changing user name
summary: Whether the login window is on the step of changing the user name.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility condition of a part of the login window.

label: Is connecting account
summary: Whether the login window is connecting an account.
details: Vanilla uses its opposite as a visibility condition in the login window, so some parts are hidden while connecting.

label: Is email sent
summary: Whether the email asked for in the login window (a password reset) has been sent.
details: Vanilla uses it together with the password restoring state and the logged in state to decide when a part of the window is shown. That it concerns the password reset email follows from that use and the name.

label: Is empty user name prompt
summary: Whether the window shows the prompt that the user name is empty.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility condition of a part of the login window.

label: Is logged in
summary: Whether the player is logged in to the account.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility condition of a part of the login window.

label: Is login step
summary: Whether the login window is on its login step.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility condition of the login part of the window. The window has other steps, such as password reset.

label: Is restoring password
summary: Whether the login window is on the step of restoring a forgotten password.
details: Vanilla uses it together with the logged in state and the email sent state to decide when a part of the window is shown.

label: Is name set
summary: Whether setting the user name has succeeded.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility condition of a part of the login window.

label: Is login info valid
summary: Whether the entered login information is acceptable.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled condition of a button in the login window, so the button works only when it is yes. What counts as valid is not shown.

label: Log in
summary: Logs in with the entered account details.
details: Vanilla calls it when return is pressed in the login window and from a click there.

label: Log out
summary: Logs the player out of the account.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the login window.

label: User name edited
summary: Handles the user name text having been edited.
details: Vanilla calls it from the edit event of the user name field in the login window. What it does with the text follows from the name only.

label: Reset password
summary: Starts the password reset for the entered email.
details: Vanilla calls it when return is pressed in the password reset field of the login window. That it sends a reset email follows from the name and the email sent check.

label: Login view itself
summary: Gives the login view object itself.
details: Going by its name and by how the same name is used on other types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set email
summary: Stores the email the player typed into the field.
details: Vanilla calls it when the text of the email field changes. It takes no value in its list, so presumably it reads the field itself.

label: Set password
summary: Stores the password the player typed into the field.
details: Vanilla calls it when the text of the password field changes. It takes no value in its list, so presumably it reads the field itself.

label: Set window step
summary: Switches the login window to another step.
details: Vanilla calls it from clicks with 'password_reset', 'login' and 'email_sent' as the step name. Other step names are not in the input.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the step to go to.

label: Set user name
summary: Confirms the user name the player typed.
details: Vanilla calls it when return is pressed in the user name field and from a click. It takes no value in its list, so presumably it reads the field itself.

label: Show login window
summary: Shows the login window.
details: Going by its name and the matching Hide function that vanilla uses. Vanilla itself does not call Show on the login view.

label: Toggle connected
summary: Switches the account between connected and not connected.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the login window. The exact effect follows from the name only.

label: Map icon itself
summary: Gives the men-at-arms origin map icon object itself.
details: Going by its name and the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Men-at-arms type

details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the icon in the map icon layer. The return type is not registered in the game's data. Reading MAA as men-at-arms is from the name.

label: Owning title
summary: The title that owns the place this map icon marks.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context in the map icon layer. The return type is not registered in the game's data; that it is a title follows from the name.

label: Province
summary: The province this map icon sits in.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context in the map icon layer. The return type is not registered in the game's data; that it is a province follows from the name.

label: Is existing location
summary: Whether the place this map icon marks exists.
details: Vanilla uses it as a visibility condition in the map icon layer: one part shows when it is yes and another when it is no.

label: Map icon itself
summary: Gives the men-at-arms origin map icon object itself.
details: Going by its name and by how the same name is used on other types. The game documents nothing more.

label: Multiplayer config itself
summary: Gives the multiplayer configuration object itself.
details: Going by its name and the many other types having the same function, it hands back the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Offline tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the offline game option.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Private tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the private game option.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the multiplayer setup window, reached through that window's multiplayer configuration (not on a bare MPConfig).

label: Public tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the public game option.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the multiplayer setup window, reached through that window's multiplayer configuration.

label: Is crossplay checked
summary: Whether the crossplay option is ticked in the multiplayer setup.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Auto-accept hot join

details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the "Auto-accept Hot Join" box in the multiplayer setup window, shown for private games; its tooltip says the host is then not asked about every player joining a game already started. The window reaches the settings through GetMPConfig.

label: Is offline
summary: Whether the multiplayer game is set to offline.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of an option in the multiplayer setup window.

label: Is private
summary: Whether the multiplayer game is set to private.
